Class platform: the tool's mixed proposal comes only from that phase-0 write. name: flags_38d75
rule: sim: a phase writes it (weak writes only)
note: Net-session handshake bits in a 16-bit word at +0x38d75 (five aliases: net_flags, flags_38d75, loadingFlags, netBits, net_bits). Bit 0 (started): set by LoadingScreenFrame (game_load.cpp). Bit 1 (loaded): set by LoadMatch (game_load.cpp). Bit 2 (start positions pending): set by LoadMatch for a network game; cleared by MainLoopTick (main_loop.cpp) and by LoadingScreenFrame once AssignStartPositions (net_game.cpp) succeeds. Bit 3 (start positions assigned): set by LoadingScreenFrame and by the harness (harness.cpp). Sim bits: 0 and 1, which DropPlayer and BroadcastPlayerLeft (net_game.cpp) read to decide whether RemovePlayer runs; and 2, which makes MainLoopTick call AssignStartPositions and which HandleNetPackets reads (as net_bits) to set shareVisionReady for packet 21. Platform: bit 3, which only the LoadMatch wait loop and DrawSyncStatus (game_load.cpp) read, and the reads of bits 0 and 1 by UpdateCdCategoryByActivity (game_dialogs.cpp) for CD audio. Class mixed because the sim bits share the word with a platform bit. Split as for uiOptionFlags: bits 0 to 2 into a sim word in the block that the load code sets through a function, bit 3 into a platform flag. The trace does not hash it: test mode has no net session, so HandleNetPackets returns at once, bit 2 is never set and DropPlayer never runs; the harness writes only bit 3.

name: g_sendCondenser
rule: mixed: a phase and presentation write it
note: Wire-level packet coalescing (NetCondenser in net_condenser.cpp): SendPacket compresses, scrambles and checksums a packet, ReceivePacket checks, expands and caches one, and the bytes that come out equal the bytes that went in. No game state: SendPacket's result reaches only SendToDPID (packets.cpp), whose caller SendFrameState ignores it, and PacketChannel::SendQueued calls SendPacketTo, which returns nothing. ReceivePacket's result (checksum failure, buffer too small) only makes PacketReceiver::ReceiveFrame (packets.cpp) drop the wire packet or retry with a larger buffer. Phases 0 to 8 reach them through BroadcastPacket; no tick code reads their fields.
